title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 108
paragraphs: From Doriscus Xerxes was pushing on to invade Greece, and as he went he compelled those he came across to join his march. For the whole country as far as Thessaly had, as I have set out before, been reduced to subjection and was tributary to the king, having been conquered by Megabazus and afterwards by Mardonius. Marching out of Doriscus, he passed first by the Samothracian strongholds, the westernmost of which is a city called Mesambria. Next comes Stryme, a city of the Thasians; between them flows the river Lisus, which at that time did not suffice to supply water for Xerxes's army but ran dry. This country was once called Gallaice, but is now called Briantice; strictly, however, it too belongs to the Cicones.
